newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fletcher earnings strong, but clouds loom for paper.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher earnings strong, but clouds loom for paper.

text.p: New Zealand's Fletcher Challenge Ltd's (FCL) divisions reported robust earnings for the June year on Wednesday but clouds may be looming for FCL Paper if pulp and paper prices remain depressed, analysts said.
If they do, the division may struggle to turn an operating profit in the current year.

While many of the profit numbers were out of kilter with forecasts, due in part to various tax treatments, the earnings before interest and tax were broadly in line with expectations for all four of FCL's "letter" stocks.
On a consolidated basis, the group's profit rose to NZ$490 million (US$340 million) from NZ$464 million.
John Cairns at Cavill White Securities said FCL Paper's second half result, which showed a significant decline in the second half, was in line with expectations.
FCL Paper produced a net profit after tax of NZ$177 million, an improvement on the year ago figure of $172 million, but a decline from the first half figure of $186 million.
The fall was due to a combination sharply lower commodity prices and production downtime.
Its share price fell six cents to NZ$2.80.
Prices for coated and uncoated woodfree papers have fallen since September 1995 by up to 25 percent.
FCL Paper's Chief Executive John Hood told a news conference that 19,000 tonnes of production in woodfree papers was foregone as downtime to keep inventories under control.
Orders from printers had picked up in recent months, but Hood said the surge may be speculative inventory building.
The price of premium grade NBSK pulp in European markets started the year at a record high of US$925 per tonne and rose to US$1,000.
But it failed to hold and by April it had collapsed to US$520 a tonne before moving up to around US$560.
"The pulp markets are barely in balance with an announced price for NBSK of US$580 still to be fully achieved," Hood said.
By June, the price of newsprint had fallen to US$685 a tonne against US$765 at the end of December. Newsprint prices at present are around US$600, and there was discounting on that.
"Newsprint is where they've got the maximum operating leverage, so they are obviously doing pretty badly there," Cavill White's Cairns said.
"For the current year I would say they would be struggling to report a profit on an operating level," he said.
Forests was suffering a similarly rigorous cyclical downturn in log prices, but the outlook was bright after the successful purchase of Forestry Corp of NZ last week.
FCL Group Chief Executive Hugh Fletcher said the purchase was likely to produce savings signficantly over NZ$18 million a year.
Likewise Building was facing a better outlook, especially now that the company has exited low margin construction.
But a problem for FCL Building was its involvement in the manufacture of medium density fibreboard (MDF), due mostly to domestic and international oversupply.
In Energy, there was an 11 percent increade in proven reserves to 127.1 million barrels of oil equivalent from 114.7 million a year earlier, a gain of 11 percnet.
"Overall you would have to say the market would have been expecting pretty much what the numbers were that came through, both pre-abnormals and post-abnormals," Stanley said.

By the close of business, Energy was up nine cents at NZ$3.40 -- its highest point since splitting as a letter stock in March. Brokers said news of strong gas flows from its Brunei operations boosted the price.
Forests firmed three to NZ$$2.03 and Building gained seven to NZ$3.26.
